name: אינטגרל מסוים של sin³(x) – בעזרת sin²=1−cos² (באנגלית)
generalfeedback:
To solve this problem we will have to express {{CT:4}} in a simpler way using some trigonometric identities <hint>trig_standard_identities</hint>

Now, recall that if \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of \(x\) then
\[\int u dv = uv - \int v du.\]

So, let \(u = {{CT:5}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}}\).

Then \(du = {{CT:7}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:8}}\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  [{{CT:5}}][{{CT:8}}] - \int [{{CT:8}}][{{CT:7}}d{{CT:3}}] +c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:10}}d{{CT:3}} +c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} + 2\int {{CT:6}}[{{CT:11}}] d{{CT:3}} +c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} + 2\int {{CT:12}} d{{CT:3}} +c
 \end{array}\]

Hence,
\[3\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:9}} + 2\int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}} +c \]

And so,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:13}}+ {{CT:14}} + \frac{c}{3} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:15}} + \frac{c}{3}.
 \end{array}\]
